direct_claims: This chart comes from a CHI 2020 paper about how participants judged whether popular apps have OSIs.
The chart compares participant response categories about whether an app has OSIs, does not have OSIs, or whether participants were unsure.
The apps shown are the top 15 most popular apps among participants, each used by at least 10% of participants.
The title and expert story indicate that recognition of OSIs differed across apps, with Discord identified as having OSIs and MyFitnessPal being known by only a few participants to have them.
The expert explanation further suggests that some of these differences may be related to how OSIs are designed within each app.
The expert story gives one concrete mechanism: Instagram's OSIs are only visible between users of the messaging feature, so awareness may depend on whether participants actually use that feature.
Because the stakeholder context is not provided, specific policy, business, or advocacy decisions supported by this chart cannot be identified with confidence.

The metadata mentions a separate Table 4 comparing a green dot experimental condition with blue, gray, and orange conditions using mean difference, SE, DF, t, p, and confidence intervals, but no table values are provided here.
Since those numerical results are absent, no valid claim can be made here about statistical significance or effect size across conditions.
The absence of the chart image, axis labels, and data table prevents identifying which other apps besides Discord, MyFitnessPal, and Instagram were included or how strongly they differed.
